statement:
The solution to the differential equation
$$\frac{dy}{dx}=|-6x|\quad\text{for all }x$$
is $y=f(x)+c$, where $c$ is a constant.

Which one of the following is a correct expression for $f(x)$?
solution:
First note $|-6x|=|6x|=6|x|$, so we integrate $6|x|$.

For $x\ge0$, $|x|=x$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=6x$ and $y=3x^2+c$.

For $x<0$, $|x|=-x$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-6x$ and $y=-3x^2+c$.

Both pieces agree at $x=0$ (both give $y=c$), so the single expression is
$$y=\begin{cases}3x^2+c & x\ge0\\ -3x^2+c & x<0\end{cases}.$$

Since $3x^2=3x\cdot x$ (for $x\ge0$) and $-3x^2=3x\cdot(-x)$ (for $x<0$), both are equal to $3x|x|$. Hence
$$f(x)=3x|x|,$$
which is **option D**.

(Check: for $x\ge0$, $\tfrac{d}{dx}(3x^2)=6x=6|x|$; for $x<0$, $\tfrac{d}{dx}(-3x^2)=-6x=6|x|$.)
hints: Note |-6x| = 6|x| and split into x≥0 and x<0.
Combine the pieces using the fact that x·|x| = x² for x≥0 and -x² for x<0.
